title: Treatise on the Heavy Sabre Arts
summary: Teaches a full-meridian student to use the sheer mass of a heavy sabre with qi for cleaving blows and an immovable stance.

title: Canon of Cut and Counter-Cut
summary: Trains the answering cut that meets an attack and returns it and builds from there a cascade of counters.

title: Discourse on Qi Beyond the Blade
summary: Shows a Xiantian student how to carry the living field of qi past the tip of the sabre for reach and sweeping force.

title: Handbook of Sabre in the Press
summary: Teaches close work with the sabre among many bodies in a hall or lane where there is little room to swing.

title: Canon of the Edge That Follows the Qi
summary: Binds the edge to the student's qi field so the blade tracks and presses and snares a foe along the flow of its own power.

title: Treatise of the Twin-Track Sabre
summary: Teaches the sabre in the dual-track manner where each cut has a paired second track that follows on the same breath.

title: Canon of the Hawk-Stoop Sabre
summary: Models the sabre on the hawk's stoop from a height with folded wing guards and a rising recovery after the strike.

title: Handbook of the River-Basin Edge
summary: Teaches the sabre as water in a basin with bends and eddies and a flood sweep and a reversal that returns a blow.

title: Discourse on the Azure Paired Cut
summary: A discourse on cuts made in azure pairs whose second stroke carries the first on to its end and closes in a sequence.

title: Handbook of the Wind-Sworn Edge
summary: Teaches the sabre cuts sworn to the wind with quick gale paces and a downrush hew and a counter that turns a gust.

title: Canon of the Plateau Bearing Cut
summary: Holds a bearing on the foe across open plateau ground and cuts along that line with qi from the field.

title: Treatise on the Sworn Gale Chop
summary: Treats the sworn chop that opens a gale oath and the parries and rebukes that break an oathbreaker's attack.

title: Discourse on the Unwalled Edge
summary: Teaches an edge that needs no cover by taking open ground and skyline and horizon as its guard and its reach.
